candidates.content_text:
Kickstart Your Career in Engineering Drafting!
Ready to turn your interest in design and engineering into a career?
Whether you’re finishing Year 12, recently left school or studying Civil Drafting at TAFE, this is your opportunity to get started in the engineering industry.
STP Consultants is looking for an enthusiastic Junior Civil Draftsperson to join our growing Brisbane team. You’ll work alongside experienced civil engineers and drafters, gain hands-on experience and learn how the drawings you create become part of real projects across Queensland.
You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, curiosity and willingness to learn.
Why you’ll love working here
Start building your career
Get hands-on experience from day one and develop practical civil drafting skills while learning from experienced engineers and drafters.
Work on real projects
Go beyond the classroom and see how civil engineering projects come together. You’ll contribute to drawings and documentation used throughout projects from concept and design through to delivery.
Learn from experienced people
Ask questions, share ideas and learn from people who genuinely want to help you develop. You’ll receive guidance and mentoring as your skills and confidence grow.
Be part of a great team
Join a close-knit, collaborative team where people support each other, work together and enjoy what they do.
Work in Fortitude Valley
Our Brisbane office is in the heart of Fortitude Valley, close to public transport, cafés, restaurants and everything the city has to offer.
The Opportunity 
As you develop your skills, you’ll have the opportunity to:
- Assist with preparing civil drawings, plans and project documentation.
- Work with engineers and experienced drafters to produce clear, accurate and high-quality drawings.
- Learn industry standards, guidelines and best-practice drafting processes.
- Develop your understanding of how civil engineering projects are designed and delivered.
- Participate in project discussions and meetings to build your understanding of project requirements.
- Carry out basic drawing and documentation checks with guidance from experienced team members.
- Take on more responsibility as your skills and confidence develop.
About you:
You could be a great fit if you are:
- A Year 12 student, recent school leaver or currently studying Civil Drafting at TAFE.
- Genuinely interested in civil drafting, design and engineering.
- Curious and keen to learn new skills.
- Detail-oriented and take pride in producing accurate work.
- A good communicator who is comfortable asking questions and taking feedback.
- Reliable, organized and willing to have a go at new challenges.
- Someone who enjoys working with others and being part of a team.
- An Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident.
Most importantly, bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn. We’ll help you turn it into a career.
What’s in it for you?
- 
Career development: Build your skills through hands-on experience, mentoring and ongoing professional development.
- 
Flexibility: Enjoy a 9-day fortnight, flexible working hours and the option to purchase additional leave.
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and contribution.
- 
Recognition and rewards: Employee referral rewards and recognition programs.
- 
Great culture: Work with supportive people in a friendly, collaborative environment, with regular team and social events.
- 
Wellbeing support: Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program.
- 
Long-term opportunity: Build your career with an established, Australian-owned engineering consultancy.
About STP Consultants 
For more than 20 years, STP Consultants has been helping shape communities across Queensland. We’re a privately owned, multidisciplinary engineering consultancy, bringing together expertise across Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Hydraulic, Fire and Seismic engineering. 
Our teams work on a diverse range of projects across Queensland, giving you the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals and see the many different paths an engineering career can take.
Our values of Potential, Respect, Integrity, Deliver and Engage shape the way we work with our clients and with each other.
We’re proud of our approachable leaders, supportive team environment and commitment to developing people and delivering quality engineering outcomes.
Ready to get started?  
If you’re looking for more than just a first job and want to build a career in engineering, we’d love to hear from you.
Click Apply and send us your Resume and Cover Letter.
In your cover letter, tell us:
1. Why you’re interested in starting a career in civil drafting.  2. What interests you about joining STP Consultants.
STP Consultants is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

Undergraduate Civil Engineer
Join the CivilPlus Team
CivilPlus Constructions is a locally owned and operated Civil & Marine Infrastructure company based in Townsville. As our business continues to grow, we are looking for a motivated 3rd or 4th Year Undergraduate Civil Engineer located in Townsville or the broader North Queensland region to join our team.
This is a great opportunity to gain valuable, hands-on experience while completing your university studies and develop your engineering career within the civil construction industry.
You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside experienced Project Managers, Engineers, Supervisors and site teams while gaining exposure to the practical delivery of civil and marine infrastructure projects throughout North Queensland.
About the Role
As an Undergraduate Engineer, you will support our project teams with the planning, coordination and delivery of civil construction projects.
This role is designed to complement your university studies by giving you practical exposure to engineering in a construction environment. You’ll gain experience across project documentation, quality, safety, environmental requirements, construction methodologies, site coordination and project reporting.
You won't just be observing, you'll have the opportunity to get involved, ask questions and develop an understanding of how projects move from plans and specifications through to construction and completion.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist Project Managers and Engineers with the day-to-day delivery of civil construction projects.
- Assist with the preparation and maintenance of project plans and documentation.
- Support the preparation of Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), work methods and project records.
- Assist with site inspections, quality documentation and construction records.
- Review and develop your understanding of construction drawings, specifications and relevant standards.
- Assist with project reporting and document control.
- Support the coordination of subcontractors, suppliers, materials and project resources.
- Attend project and site meetings where required.
- Assist with Quality, Safety and Environmental requirements across projects.
- Gain exposure to contract administration, procurement and project commercial processes.
- Communicate with Engineers, Supervisors and site personnel to support project activities.
- Assist with maintaining CivilPlus' Project and Business Management Systems.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will:
- Be currently studying a Bachelor of Civil Engineering and be in your 3rd or 4th year of study.
- Have a genuine interest in pursuing a career within the civil construction industry.
- Be eager to gain practical, hands-on engineering and construction experience.
- Have strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Be organised with good attention to detail.
- Have good computer skills, particularly Microsoft Office.
- Be willing to learn and take direction from experienced members of the project team.
- Have a proactive attitude and be comfortable asking questions.
- Be able to work both independently and as part of a team.
- Have strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to develop your technical knowledge.
- Hold a current Driver Licence.
Location & Availability
This opportunity is open to candidates located in Townsville and the broader North Queensland region.
Due to the practical nature of the role, applicants will need to have suitable availability to attend CivilPlus worksites, offices and operational activities as required.
The position will involve a combination of site-based and office-based experience, providing exposure to the day-to-day delivery of civil and marine infrastructure projects across North Queensland.
Candidates should hold a current Driver Licence and be comfortable travelling to project locations as required.
What We Offer
- The opportunity to gain real-world civil construction experience while completing your degree.
- Exposure to a diverse range of civil and marine infrastructure projects.
- Hands-on experience both on site and within project delivery teams.
- Mentoring and support from experienced Project Managers, Engineers and Supervisors.
- Exposure to project planning, construction, quality, safety, environmental and commercial aspects of project delivery.
- Opportunity to develop practical skills that complement your university studies.
- A supportive and team-oriented workplace.
- The opportunity to build a career with CivilPlus following completion of your studies.
How to Apply
If you're a 3rd or 4th Year Civil Engineering student looking to take what you're learning at university and apply it to real construction projects, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply via SEEK or email your resume and cover letter to admin@civilplus.com.au.
CivilPlus Constructions is committed to delivering quality civil and marine infrastructure while supporting the development of the next generation of construction professionals.

About the Opportunity 
As part of the Infrastructure Program, the Graduate Civil Engineer will contribute to projects that help shape how people move through, connect with and experience the City of Adelaide. You'll gain practical experience across the planning, design and delivery of civil infrastructure projects, working alongside experienced engineers and project teams.
From roads, footpaths and drainage to water sensitive urban design and transport infrastructure, you'll be exposed to a diverse range of projects and challenges. You'll also build experience working with consultants, contractors and a broad range of stakeholders, giving you an understanding of the project lifecycle from concept through to delivery.
This is an opportunity to turn your university knowledge into real-world experience, develop your technical and project skills and start building a career in an environment where your work can have a visible impact on the city around you.
To view a copy of the position description, please click here.
Working Rights - Eligibility
We welcome applications from candidates with valid Australian work rights, including those holding a visa with sufficient and appropriate work rights for the position. Australian citizenship is not required; however, visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
About You
To be successful in this role you will have:
 - Graduated within approximately the last two years or are expecting to graduate within approximately the next 6 months in Civil Engineering.
 - Eligible to join Engineers Australia as a Graduate Engineer (GradIEAust) upon completion of tertiary qualification.
 - Knowledge of the principles and practice of civil engineering, and emerging trends, principles and operations with an understanding of civil engineering operations and function.
 - Knowledge of Australian standards, codes of practice, authority regulations and accepted industry best practice for the design and installation of engineering services associated with Civil Engineering projects and Local Government public realm projects.
 - Skills and knowledge in conducting research to inform best practice and evidence-based approaches.
 - Ability to provide welcoming, responsive and respectful customer service to colleagues and community members, with a commitment to continuous learning, professional development and applying feedback.
 - Ability to take ownership and accountability for deliverables.
 - Skilled in communication and being able to present effectively both orally and written.
 - Strong organisational skills, the ability to successfully manage competing priorities, maintain attention to detail and meet deadlines.
Why Our Graduate Program?
Our graduate program gives you a great opportunity to start building your career, while having our genuine impact on our City and our communities. As a capital city council, we have wide-ranging responsibilities, so you'll be exposed to many different industries. This includes everything from community wellbeing to urban planning, events to infrastructure, lifestyle experiences to heritage, economic development to climate action, corporate services and many more.
Apart from gaining valuable insight into what makes our community unique, are entitled to a wide range of benefits such as:
 - Flexible work arrangements
 - A range of health & wellbeing offerings
 - On-site gym and chill-out areas
 - Social Club events where you get to connect with other colleagues

 - Mentorship: You'll be partnered with a City of Adelaide leader who will provide guidance and support throughout your first year.

 - Regular check-ins: You'll have regular 1:1 conversation with your leader to ensure ongoing support, goal setting, wellbeing checks and guidance.
 - Hone your skills: Opportunities to develop a broad range of transferable skills relevant to various government roles federal, state and local. 
 - Networking opportunities: within the City Council and the broader government sector. 
For more information about what it's like to work for the City of Adelaide, including the benefits, please visit www.cityofadelaide.com.au/careers
About Us
Located in the geographic heart of Kaurna Country, the City of Adelaide celebrates its cultural heritage, unique natural surrounds and structures its footprint in a way that allows it to adapt to the changing needs of the community and a dynamic global landscape. Our focus is on our community's wellbeing and quality of life - investing in city improvements and on future planning, so we continue to design a liveable city where future generations can continue to live authentic and meaningful lives. This is an exciting opportunity to join our team and be a bigger part of our amazing city!
At the City of Adelaide, we thrive in an environment that is welcoming, inclusive and safe, and celebrates difference. We value and embrace our diverse perspectives and recognise the value diversity has in fuelling innovation and enabling brilliant experiences for our diverse community.

Location: Rockhampton
Remuneration/Benefit: Industry-leading Enterprise Agreement remuneration, including overtime and penalty rate entitlements, supported by strong career development opportunities.
Aurizon is seeking a Project Engineer to join the Construction Management team within Network.
Why join our team?
- You'll work in one of the most dynamic sectors of construction. Rail closures are high-pressure, high-consequence environments where success comes from quality planning, teamwork and execution. The rewards are seeing your work delivered in real time and being part of a team trusted to keep critical freight infrastructure operating.
- Enjoy long-term stability and certainty. Unlike many project delivery roles, you'll be part of a permanent team with a predictable pipeline of work and visibility of planned projects well into the future.
- Be home most nights. This is not a FIFO or project-hopping contractor role. You'll have the opportunity to build a career while maintaining a lifestyle outside of work.
- Plan your life with confidence. Our forward work program provides visibility of major works and shutdowns, allowing you to better coordinate leave, family commitments and personal interests.
- Join a close-knit, high-performing team that supports one another and takes pride in delivering challenging projects safely and successfully.
About the Role:
In this role, you'll be responsible for managing the delivery of rail infrastructure projects across Aurizon's CQCN network, from initial customer engagement and project development through to construction and handover.
Working closely with customers, operations, maintenance teams, contractors and industry stakeholders, you'll develop project scopes, delivery strategies, programs and budgets, while providing technical leadership throughout the project lifecycle.
This is a hands-on role that combines engineering, project management and field leadership. You'll spend time both in the office and on site, overseeing construction activities, managing project risks, ensuring compliance with safety and environmental requirements, and driving project outcomes that deliver value for our customers and the business.
You'll join a highly experienced team delivering a diverse portfolio of rail infrastructure projects, offering the opportunity to take ownership of meaningful works, develop strong industry relationships and build a long-term career within Aurizon.
Other responsibilities will include but aren’t limited to: 
- Delivering asset renewal projects, maintenance and external projects covering general earthworks, formation, bridges, culverts, level crossings and other rail-associated works. 
- Provide support to project team throughout the entire project lifecycle, from tendering to project completion. 
- Collaborate with multi-disciplinary teams to identify and resolve delivery roadblocks and escalate when required. 
- Provide advice in relation to project planning and develop project cost estimates, risk assessments, development of construction methods, procedures and programs when required. 
- Managing Contractor’s safety performance, project progress, conformance with scope of work, contract deliverables, quality standards and specifications. 
- Provide support and supervision to field operations, ensuring work complies with quality, safety, environmental standards and other relevant standards and legislation and foster a culture of excellence in project outcomes. 
- Identifying design and constructability issues and assist in providing the most efficient solution. 
About you:  
- Bachelor of Engineering (Civil preferred). 
- CPEng/RPEQ qualifications (or working towards). 
- Current Class C Drivers Licence (mandatory). 
- Ideally 5 years' experience in project delivery across mid to large-scale civil projects (essential). 
- High level of skill in planning, organising, and programming of infrastructure construction projects. 
- Familiarity with WHS and Environmental legislation and ability to produce Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS), understand company Quality procedures and WHS Act. 
- Strong level of computer skills, including Microsoft and Primavera (preferred). 
- Excellent interpersonal, communication and negotiation skills both written and verbal. 
- Willing to commit to travel as needed and willing to relocate to Rockhampton for the role (NO FIFO/DIDO). 
- A self-starter with a strong work ethic, accountability and ownership mindset, who proactively drives solutions and delivers outcomes with minimal supervision.
 What we offer you:      
At Aurizon, we support the development and growth of our employees. With a national portfolio of operations, we offer long-term and exciting career opportunities. 
Some of our benefits include:
- Development and growth opportunities.
- Access to mentoring and development programs.
- Discounts on selected health insurance funds, personal travel, gyms, vehicles and retail brands.
- Parental leave program and super booster.
About Aurizon.
Aurizon is Australia’s largest rail freight operator and a top 100 ASX company. Each year, we deliver more than 250 million tonnes of Australian commodities right across the country. Aurizon is crucial to the Australian economy, connecting miners, primary producers and industry with international and domestic markets.
Look to Aurizon for a diverse and collaborative culture.
At Aurizon, we are proud of our diverse, collaborative, creative and high-performance culture. We celebrate the contribution of every employee and provide opportunities for career development in a dynamic, caring, and inclusive work environment.
To learn about us and our company values, please visit www.aurizon.com.au/careers

Empower Management has been retained by a well-established Queensland civil contractor delivering TMR and Council road infrastructure across Brisbane and South East Queensland. - Structures and bridges
- Services and utilities
- Concrete and associated civil works

- Identifying project risks and commercial opportunities early

- A clear individual development pathway
- Exposure across technical, operational and commercial project delivery
- Genuine opportunities to take on more responsibility as you prove yourself
- Strong project pipeline across Brisbane and SEQ
- Competitive salary package
- Two project-based bonus/performance schemes
- Family-friendly environment
- A practical, low-politics culture where good people are backed
There’s no interest here in keeping a capable engineer in the same box for five years.
If you perform, you’ll get more responsibility.
What You’ll Bring
- Civil Engineering degree or equivalent
- Around 4-5+ years of civil construction experience
·        TMR experience will obviously be highly regarded, but equally important is your attitude toward development and taking responsibility.
- Good understanding of civil construction methodology
- Working knowledge of QA, ITPs, RFIs, programming and project documentation
- Exposure to cost control, procurement and subcontractor management
- Ability to read drawings, specifications and project contracts
- Strong communication skills with both site and client-facing teams
- A practical, solutions-focused approach
- Genuine ambition to progress into project management
This is a smart move for a Project Engineer
seeking stability, challenge, broad experience and genuine career momentum in a
high-value, low-politics environment.

candidates.content_text:
Civil Engineer – Sydney, NSW 
About Indus Engineering Pty Ltd
Indus Engineering Pty Ltd is a leading engineering and construction firm specialising in infrastructure and civil projects across Australia. Our team provides design services and project management services for civil infrastructure projects.
We are currently seeking a versatile and multi-skilled Civil Engineer to join our team in Sydney. The ideal candidate will be a adaptable professional capable of multitasking across diverse technical areas, including preparing civil design, Primavera P6 project scheduling, first-principles cost estimation, and on-site project execution.
Key Responsibilities:
- Design, plan, develop, and oversee civil engineering works, including pipelines, drainage, structural, and infrastructure projects.
- Prepare engineering drawings, specifications, and cost estimates.
- Develop and maintain project work programs using Primavera P6 / MS Project.
- Perform quantity take-offs  and BOQ reconciliation for civil works.
- Analyse project risks, prepare technical specifications, and manage variation orders and Extension of Time (EOT) evaluations.
- Conduct site inspections, technical assessments, and feasibility studies to ensure compliance with Australian Standards, WHS, and building codes.
- Prepare Construction Methodologies technical specifications and ensuring compliance with Australian standards and local regulations 
-  Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including structural, electrical, and environmental engineers 
- Utilise AutoCAD and other engineering software to prepare detailed design.
- Assist in the procurement of subcontractors and materials based on project requirements 
- Identify and resolve potential engineering challenges.
- Collaborate with project managers, client representatives, contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams to deliver high-quality outcomes.
Skills & Experience Required:
- Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field.
- Minimum 3+ years of experience in civil engineering projects.
- Strong knowledge of AutoCAD and relevant engineering software.
- Strong knowledge of civil project controls, cost estimation, project scheduling, or design methodologies.
- Understanding of Australian Standards, WHS regulations, and building codes.
- Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills.
- Ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
- Prior experience in major civil infrastructure and water/wastewater networks projects is highly desirable.
What We Offer:
✔ Competitive salary ($85,000 - $110,000 + Super)
✔ Career development & professional growth opportunities
✔ Opportunity to work on diverse and large-scale civil projects
✔ Supportive and collaborative work culture
How to Apply:
Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by sending their resume and cover letter to admin@indusengineering.com.au or via SEEK. Indus Engineering Pty Ltd is an equal opportunity employer, and we encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply.

We offer flexible career life balance with hours that allow you to relax and recharge. We offer a variety of flexible work arrangement options (e.g. flexible hours and working from home) where appropriate giving you even greater quality of work life balance.

The Student/Graduate Engineer (Road Access) plays an important role in supporting the management of works within the public domain and protecting Council's road, footpath, cycling and stormwater infrastructure. Ready for your next move? 
Join STP Consultants as a Civil Engineer and become part of our growing Brisbane team, delivering a diverse range of projects across Queensland. You'll work on challenging engineering solutions, take ownership of your work and collaborate with experienced professionals across a multidisciplinary consultancy.
This is an opportunity to broaden your technical experience, contribute to meaningful projects and play an important role in the continued development of our Brisbane office.
Why you’ll love working here 
A growing team with exciting opportunities
Be part of a supportive team where your experience, ideas and contribution are valued. As our Brisbane office expands, you'll have the opportunity to build strong professional relationships, share your knowledge and make a meaningful contribution to our continued success.
Variety that builds your experience
Work across residential, commercial and infrastructure projects, gaining exposure to a range of engineering challenges across Queensland. From developing technical solutions to supporting project delivery, you'll have the opportunity to apply your skills across diverse projects and continue expanding your experience.
Take ownership of your career
Develop your technical capabilities, take on greater responsibility and learn from experienced engineers and designers. Depending on your experience and interests, you'll have opportunities to lead projects, mentor developing professionals and strengthen your client relationships.
A great Brisbane location
Our Fortitude Valley office is conveniently located close to public transport, cafés and restaurants, with easy access to the CBD, New Farm and Howard Smith Wharves. Enjoy a convenient work location while being part of a team delivering quality engineering solutions.
What's in it for you? 
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and the value you bring. 
- 
Flexibility: 9-day fortnight, flexible hours, plus the option to purchase additional leave. 
- 
Professional development: CPD support, mentoring and opportunities to build your technical expertise.
- 
Recognition and rewards: Employee referral rewards and recognition programs that celebrate your contribution.
- 
Inclusive, friendly culture: Supportive colleagues, collaborative working relationships and regular social events. 
- 
Wellbeing support: Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
- 
Career growth: Opportunities to take ownership of your work, develop your skills and progress within STP.
- 
Stability & reputation: Join a respected, Australian-owned consultancy with a strong and diverse client base. 
The opportunity 
As our Brisbane office continues to grow, we’re looking for an experienced Civil Engineer to join our team and help deliver exciting projects across Queensland. 
In this role, you will:
- Deliver civil engineering projects from concept and feasibility through to design and construction 
- Undertake technical and feasibility studies, including site investigations and assessments 
- Prepare detailed civil designs and engineering reports for industrial, commercial and land development projects 
- Design roads, drainage, earthworks and flexible and rigid pavements 
- Develop stormwater management solutions, including flood modelling and civil DA documentation 
- Prepare tender, design and construction documentation 
- Conduct civil site inspections and provide construction support to ensure quality project outcomes 
- Collaborate with clients, consultants and multidisciplinary teams to coordinate and resolve design solutions 
- Assist with project planning, budgets, quality assurance and delivery 
- Build strong client relationships and contribute to successful project outcomes 
- Support and share knowledge with junior engineers and designers 
- Contribute to the continued growth of our Brisbane team 
About you
- Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering or equivalent. 
- Minimum 5 years' experience in a similar role, preferable within a consulting environment 
- Experience with 12D, AutoCAD, DRAINS, MUSIC or XPStorm will be highly regarded 
- Strong knowledge of Australian Standards, planning frameworks, engineering codes and local authority requirements 
- Strong stormwater, flood modelling and pavement design knowledge  
- RPEQ registration (or ability to gain) is highly desirable. 
- Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in a team. 
- Australian Citizenship or Permanent Residency 
About STP Consultants   
For more than 20 years, STP Consultants has been helping shape communities across Queensland. As a privately owned, multidisciplinary consultancy, we bring together expertise in Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Hydraulic, Fire and Seismic engineering to deliver a diverse range of projects across the state. 
Our values - Potential, Respect, Integrity, Deliver and Engage, guide how we work with our clients and support one another every day.  
We’re proud of our approachable leaders, collaborative culture and commitment to technical excellence. At STP, you’ll work alongside experienced professionals in an environment where people are trusted to contribute, share ideas and deliver quality outcomes. 
If you're looking for a role that offers project variety, professional growth, a supportive team and the opportunity to be part of a growing Brisbane office, we'd love to hear from you.
Click Apply Now and join the STP Consultants team in Brisbane.

Recognised by the AFR as a Best Place to Work in 2026, we embrace diverse perspectives, giving you the opportunity to make a real impact.

We believe the world needs people who can engineer possibilities; people who can create infrastructure that makes life better for people and the planet. candidates.content_text:
Civil Project Engineer
- Opportunity to work with Rio Tinto
- Ongoing assignment via Chandler Macleod
- Safety-first culture with supportive teams
 About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.
Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Civil Project Engineer to join Rio Tinto’s One Gladstone Self-Perform team, supporting annual wall raise programs across QAL and Yarwun. You will play a key role in the safe planning and delivery of sustaining capital civil and earthworks projects while working closely with project, construction and operational teams.
Key Responsibilities
- Support the planning and execution of annual wall raise programs.
- Manage civil work packages through the full project lifecycle.
- Coordinate engineering, procurement, construction and specialist resources.
- Monitor project schedules, budgets, forecasts and construction performance.
- Provide field engineering support and resolve technical delivery challenges.
- Manage project risks, design changes, technical queries and change control.
- Support procurement, contract administration, reporting and capital governance requirements.
- Work closely with Operations, Engineering and Construction teams to achieve safe and successful project outcomes.
About You
- Delivery-focused Civil Project Engineer with hands-on civil construction and earthworks experience; this is not a structural design-focused role.
- Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering (or equivalent) with eligibility for professional engineering registration.
- 8+ years' experience delivering civil earthworks and infrastructure projects within mining, resources, heavy industry or major infrastructure environments.
- Strong project controls, field engineering, stakeholder engagement and EPC coordination capability.
- Demonstrated commitment to safety, quality and successful project delivery.
- Current residence in the Gladstone region is essential. FIFO arrangements and relocation assistance are not available for this role.
- Current Australian driver's licence and ability to pass pre-employment medical testing. SAP, Microsoft Project or self-perform delivery experience is highly regarded.
Why Join Chandler Macleod?
Chandler Macleod is one of Australia’s most experienced workforce partners. You’ll receive a competitive pay rate paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, support from a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.
Apply Now!
Ready to take the next step? Apply today to join Chandler Macleod for an exciting onsite assignment with Rio Tinto.
At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse people, people living with disability and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

About the role
Vorstrom Vacuum Equipment is looking for a Cadet Draftperson to join the design and engineering team in Warwick. This is an opportunity for someone leaving school or early in their career to start a career in engineering drafting. You will be supported and trained through a Certificate IV in Engineering Drafting, with on-the-job training across the range of vacuum trucks and tankers. Applicants who are completing or have completed a Certificate IV are also encouraged to apply.
Key responsibilities
- Preparation and revision of engineering drawings under supervision
- Learning to read and interpret drawings, specifications and bills of materials
- Using CAD software (Solidworks) to create and update drawings and models
- Complete a Certificate IV in Engineering Drafting
- Liaise with the engineering, production and workshop teams
- Potential to support the commissioning team
About you
- School leavers (or soon to be) welcome
- Also open to those completing (or have completed) Certificate IV in Engineering Drafting (or similar)
- Attention to detail and desire to learn
- Comfortable using computers
- Previous CAD experience is a bonus (but not required)
- Able to work well in a team
- Interest in engineering/design/mechanical equipment
Benefits
- Full support and sponsorship to start or continue a nationally recognised Certificate IV in Engineering Drafting
- On-the-job mentoring from an experienced drafting and engineering team
- Hands-on experience across real projects in vacuum equipment design and manufacturing
- Potential to expand duties to suit as experience grows
- A genuine long-term career pathway within the business
- A supportive, local Warwick-based workplace
https://vorstrom.com.au

candidates.abstract: TMR has a vacancy for a civil engineer to join our Maintenance Team based in Bundaberg.

candidates.location: Bundaberg, Bundaberg & Wide Bay Burnett QLD
bullets: Permanent full time with flexible work options
$3,941.00 to $4,292.00 per fortnight plus super and leave loading benefits

candidates.content_text:
With supervision and guidance from senior engineering staff, you will project manage the delivery of road infrastructure projects through the administration of contracts and provision of technical expertise and support to the design, construction and
maintenance processes.
Some of your responsibilities will include:
•  Administer road and bridge maintenance contracts to ensure compliance and successful delivery to Transport & Main Roads specifications.
•  Identify possible problem areas and negotiate modifications or adaptations to design briefs where necessary to achieve acceptance.
•  Calculate quantities of component materials, analyse test results for materials, identify non-conformances, determine the controls needed during construction, and conduct and manage risk assessment.
•  Manage under supervision, projects or elements of projects and provide monthly financial forecasting.
•  Maintain communication and alliances with stakeholders, manage expectations and issues, and identify possible political and high risk matters to ensure they are dealt with in a timely and professional manner.
Requirements of the role:
•  Engineering Operations - Applies a professional input to the operation of engineering activities under guidance.
•  Coordinate response to road network impacts through the application of processes, systems, and resourcing to enable the safe and efficient operation of the road network.
• Contract Administration - Applies an understanding of contract administration to administer construction contracts.
• Project Management - Applies project management principles and methodology to achieve project outcomes for construction projects.
• Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with both internal and external stakeholders to enable the collaborative delivery of customer-focused outcomes.
Mandatory qualifications and conditions:
• A four-year, Washington Accord accredited, Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) or equivalence which is assessed/accepted by Engineers Australia against Washington Accord benchmarks.
• Current C class drivers licence.
• Due to this role having access to sensitive data, a criminal history check will be conducted on the recommended person for this role.
Why choose TMR? We offer:
• Annual Registered Professional Engineers Queensland (RPEQ) compensation payment of $8,200 - where applicable.
• Annual reimbursement of professional fees.
• Annual health & wellbeing reimbursement of $109.40.
• Corporate discounts from a range of leading private health companies.
• Further learning and development support available through the Study and Research Assistance Scheme (SARAS).
• Relocation assistance.
• 4 weeks annual leave + 17.5% annual leave loading.
Applications to remain current for 12 months.
Job Ad Reference: QLD/702317/26
Closing Date: Thursday, 08 October 2026

bullets: Options to work in Gold Coast or Brisbane offices
Expert team to learn from and grow
Accelerated growth

candidates.content_text:
About Us
Durack Civil is a growing and progressive civil construction business delivering road, bridge and infrastructure projects for local and state government clients across Queensland, New South Wales and the Northern Territory.
Beyond our core civil operations, the Durack Group continues to expand into land development and other exciting ventures, creating long-term opportunities for our people. As our business continues to grow, we are seeking an experienced Civil Estimator to join our high-performing team and play a key role in securing and delivering future projects.
The Opportunity
Based on the Gold Coast or Brisbane, this role will see you working closely with our pre-contracts and project delivery teams to prepare accurate, competitive and well-considered estimates across a diverse range of civil infrastructure projects.
This is an opportunity to join a dynamic and ambitious business where your experience and input will directly influence project outcomes and company growth.
Qualifications & Experience
- Tertiary or trade qualifications in Construction, Engineering, Quantity Surveying, Project Management or a related discipline.
- Demonstrated experience across multiple sectors of the civil construction industry, including urban infrastructure, transport, resources, DTMR and/or slope stabilisation projects.
- Minimum 6 years' experience in civil construction, with site-based experience highly regarded.
- Previous estimating experience with a mid-tier civil contractor operating in Queensland, New South Wales and/or the Northern Territory.
- Strong project planning and programming capabilities, including proficiency with MS Project.
- Excellent attention to detail, commercial acumen and communication skills.
Key Responsibilities
- Prepare accurate first-principles estimates for civil and structural construction projects.
- Source quotations and manage procurement activities during the tender phase.
- Develop construction methodologies, tender programs and non-price submission documentation.
- Lead and coordinate the pre-contract phase of project opportunities.
- Assist project teams with cost monitoring, forecasting and commercial support during project delivery.
- Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across estimating and tendering functions.
Why Join Durack Civil?
- Join a business experiencing strong and sustained growth.
- Be part of a collaborative, energetic and solutions-focused team.
- Work on diverse and challenging infrastructure projects.
- Enjoy genuine opportunities for career progression and professional development.
- Competitive remuneration package aligned with experience and expertise.
